changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments leaders who build the case for a CFO: lead with their own numbers. Example: "See your approvals by market, with the reasons behind each decline, and the money left on the table in each country." Use "approvals", not "authorization". If the average uplift appears at all, put it in a footnote, never in the headline.
changes.why: The average uplift in the Authorization Boost deck was rejected outright ("that's an average. What's mine?"; "I can't take an average to my CFO."), while the customer-specific analysis was called the most useful thing we sent.

changes.change: For accounts where a new payments leader has taken over, or where a competitor is pitching local acquiring: proactively offer a market-by-market view of their own approval rates, broken out by country, card type and issuer, with the reason for each gap. Offer it before they pull the numbers themselves, and do not wait for them to ask.
changes.why: The new head of payments started by pulling declines by country, Adyen won by testing his own traffic and reporting results by country, and our version of that view arrived three weeks after he asked, when the test was already finished.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For payments leaders: "A named person at Stripe reviews your approval rates every month." Pair it with a stated turnaround time for market-by-market analysis. A person must confirm the turnaround before this is published.
changes.why: The buyer asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name. Tiered ticket response times answer a question he never asked.
